The sales guy there was funny and cool and suggested I just try them all until I found one that fit me really well, because an excellent fit is important. So I did. That day, I was wearing my helmet, gloves, and leathers. I was also wearing a special jacket that isn't made from leather, but has Kevlar in it. On top of this, I was wearing riding boots and my body armor. I got that idea from my son who was into mountain bike racing. One of these days, I'll tell you about that.

Now, seeing as we're just digressing, I hate boats. Boats are fine, when they belong to other people.

You know how they say you can't sink canoes? That's a lie. I have two of them that are missing. One, I watched sink. The other, just disappeared. I presume it sunk. However, I didn't witness that. I was too busy swimming to an island and lamenting my lost drugs and alcohol. A buddy had stood up in the canoe. The lost one was getting swamped with like a 10' swell. It was probably bigger. It's a big lake.

So, I took lessons in sailing. I even took two courses at the Maritime Academy. I bought a 23 footer. I took it out on the lake. The wind picked up. It was pure sail operated. I tried to hit the dock for like three hours. Finally, I rammed that fucker right into the shore and put a for sale sign on it, along with the trailer. I only took that boat out once.

It sold really quickly. I don't know why. You might just as well go down to the shore and throw that money right straight into the water. That will save time and possible your life.

With that money, I bought a fancy bass boat. You can imagine how much I spent on the boat, because it was just about the same amount I made from selling the sailboat...

I spent all winter working on it. I never even out it in the water. I added every gizmo you can imagine. It even had a fridge for beer.

I go down to fill it with gas. I leave it at the pump. I'd never had it in the water. That's important...

Some kid's parents went in the store and she was to pull up to the tanks and pump the gas for their car. Instead, she rammed right into the back of my bass boat. She pushed the hull in a good two feet. I didn't even claim it on my insurance. Instead, I put it in a storage facility. I've never even priced the repair.

It serves as a good reminder to not buy another boat. Boats are awful.

If you sailed freshwater, I'd say bring your boat and come visit. We do have some big lakes. The only good thing about boats is the knots you tie. Use them to tie me up, if I'm ever thinking about buying another boat. Satellite image Rangeley, Maine, and then work your way out.
